rounds.t: Thyroid development, thyroglossal duct, and ectopic thyroid

q.s: A 6-year-old girl has a painless 1.5-cm mass in the anterior midline of the neck just below the hyoid bone. The mass rises when she protrudes her tongue. What is the most likely diagnosis?
e: Cystic hygromas are lymphatic malformations, usually in the posterior triangle, and do not move with the tongue.
Correct. A persistent thyroglossal duct forms an anterior midline cyst that moves with swallowing or tongue protrusion because the tract is attached to the tongue base.
A dermoid can be midline but does not elevate with tongue protrusion.
Pharyngeal cleft cysts lie in the lateral neck, anterior to the sternocleidomastoid, and do not move with tongue protrusion.
A thyroid nodule moves with swallowing but sits lower, in the gland, and does not rise with tongue protrusion.

q.s: From which embryologic structure does the thyroid diverticulum arise?
e: The thyroid begins on the floor, not the roof, of the primitive pharynx.
Correct. The thyroid diverticulum arises from the floor of the primitive pharynx and descends into the neck.
The 3rd pouch forms the thymus and inferior parathyroids.
Neural crest gives rise to parafollicular C cells in some schemes, but the gland itself starts as a pharyngeal floor diverticulum.
Rathke pouch, from oral ectoderm, forms the anterior pituitary.

q.s: The normal adult remnant of the thyroglossal duct, seen as a small pit on the dorsum of the tongue, is the:
e: The lingual tonsil is lymphoid tissue, unrelated to thyroid descent.
The sulcus terminalis is the V-shaped groove behind which the foramen cecum lies; it is not itself the duct remnant.
Correct. The foramen cecum is the normal remnant of the thyroglossal duct at the tongue base.
Vallate papillae are taste structures anterior to the sulcus terminalis.
A pyramidal lobe is a persistent distal thyroglossal duct remnant, not the normal tongue pit.

q.s: A 34-year-old woman undergoes thyroidectomy. The surgeon notes a thin superior extension of thyroid tissue rising from the isthmus toward the hyoid. This structure most likely represents:
o: A persistent distal thyroglossal duct (pyramidal lobe)
e: A node would not be a continuous lobe of normal thyroid tissue.
Correct. The thyroglossal duct can persist as cysts or as the pyramidal lobe of the thyroid.
2nd cleft remnants lie laterally along the sternocleidomastoid.
Thymic remnants descend toward the mediastinum, not up to the hyoid.
Parathyroid tissue sits on the posterior thyroid surface, not as a superior midline extension.

q.s: A 9-year-old boy has a firm, round, reddish mass at the base of his tongue causing dysphagia. Thyroid scintigraphy shows uptake only in the mass, with no tissue in the neck. What is the most important risk of surgically removing the mass?
e: Correct. A lingual thyroid may be the only functioning thyroid tissue; removing it causes hypothyroidism.
Parathyroids develop from pharyngeal pouches and descend into the neck separately.
Thyroid storm is a hyperthyroid crisis, not a consequence of removing the only thyroid tissue.
Removing thyroid tissue does not cause hypercalcemia.
The lingual mass is far from the recurrent laryngeal nerves.

q.s: What is the most common site of ectopic thyroid tissue?
e: Struma ovarii is thyroid tissue in an ovarian teratoma, a rare site.
Mediastinal thyroid is usually a substernal goiter extension, less common than lingual thyroid.
This is not a recognized common site of ectopic thyroid.
Lateral neck thyroid tissue suggests metastatic thyroid cancer until proven otherwise.
Correct. The tongue (lingual thyroid) is the most common site of ectopic thyroid tissue.

q.s: A child has a midline neck mass. Which physical finding best distinguishes a thyroglossal duct cyst from a pharyngeal cleft cyst?
o: Movement with swallowing or tongue protrusion in the midline
Presence of a sinus opening on the skin
e: Size does not distinguish the two.
Both cysts can become tender if infected.
Correct. Thyroglossal duct cysts are midline and move with swallowing or tongue protrusion; pharyngeal cleft cysts are lateral and fixed.
Sinus tracts can occur with cleft anomalies but are not the defining difference.
Both fluid-filled cysts may transilluminate.

q.s: A 25-year-old man has a painless mass in the lateral neck anterior to the sternocleidomastoid that does not move with swallowing. What is the most likely origin?
e: 4th pouch derivatives are the superior parathyroids and parafollicular cells, not lateral neck cysts.
A thyroglossal duct cyst is midline and moves with swallowing.
Correct. A persistent cervical sinus leads to a pharyngeal cleft cyst in the lateral neck.
Lingual thyroid is at the tongue base.
The pyramidal lobe is midline, rising from the isthmus.

q.s: Thyroid follicular cells, which make thyroglobulin and T4, are derived from which germ layer?
e: Surface ectoderm forms epidermis and the anterior pituitary (via oral ectoderm), not follicular cells.
Neuroectoderm forms the posterior pituitary and CNS.
Neural crest forms the adrenal medulla and contributes C cells, not follicular cells.
Correct. Thyroid follicular cells are derived from endoderm of the pharyngeal floor.
Mesoderm forms the adrenal cortex and connective tissue, not thyroid follicles.

q.s: A 48-year-old woman has a thyroid nodule. Biopsy shows a tumor arising from cells that secrete calcitonin. Embryologically, these cells come from which structure?
e: Correct. Parafollicular (C) cells, which secrete calcitonin and give rise to medullary carcinoma, arise from the 4th pharyngeal pouch (ultimobranchial body).
The 3rd pouch forms the thymus and inferior parathyroids.
The 1st cleft forms the external auditory meatus.
The pharyngeal floor gives rise to follicular cells.
The 2nd pouch forms the epithelial lining of the palatine tonsil.

q.s: During embryonic descent, the developing thyroid remains attached to the tongue by which structure?
e: The stomodeum is the primitive mouth.
The urachus connects the bladder to the umbilicus.
The ductus arteriosus connects the pulmonary artery and aorta.
The vitelline duct connects the midgut to the yolk sac.
Correct. The thyroglossal duct connects the descending thyroid to the tongue and normally disappears.

q.s: A 7-year-old has a midline neck cyst excised. To minimize recurrence, the surgeon removes the tract along with the central portion of which structure?
e: The mandible is far from the tract.
Correct. The thyroglossal duct passes in close relation to the hyoid, so the middle of the hyoid is excised with the tract to prevent recurrence.
The tract passes near, but the bone excised in the Sistrunk procedure is the hyoid.
The cricoid lies below the thyroid cartilage and is not involved.
The manubrium lies below the thyroid gland.

q.s: Which statement about the thyroglossal duct is correct?
o: It normally persists into adulthood as a patent canal
It gives rise to the parathyroid glands
It connects the thyroid to the esophagus
It normally involutes, leaving the foramen cecum on the tongue
e: The duct normally disappears; only the foramen cecum remains.
Parafollicular cells arise from the 4th pharyngeal pouch.
Parathyroids arise from the 3rd and 4th pharyngeal pouches.
It connects the thyroid to the tongue.
Correct. The duct normally disappears; the foramen cecum is its normal remnant.

q.s: A newborn has congenital hypothyroidism on screening. Imaging finds a small round focus of thyroid tissue at the base of the tongue and no gland in the neck. Which developmental process failed?
o: Descent of the thyroid diverticulum along the thyroglossal duct
e: Neural crest migration forms C cells and the adrenal medulla.
4th pouch failure would affect C cells and superior parathyroids, not thyroid descent.
Rathke pouch forms the anterior pituitary.
Palatine fusion forms the secondary palate.
Correct. Failure of descent leaves thyroid tissue at the tongue base (lingual thyroid), often insufficient and causing hypothyroidism.

q.s: A 40-year-old woman has medullary thyroid carcinoma. Which serum marker reflects the embryologic cell of origin of this tumor?
e: Thyroglobulin is made by follicular cells and is a marker for papillary and follicular carcinoma.
Anti-TPO is an autoimmune marker, not a tumor marker.
PTH comes from parathyroid chief cells.
Correct. Medullary carcinoma arises from parafollicular C cells (4th pouch), which secrete calcitonin.
TSH is a pituitary hormone.

q.s: Which pair correctly matches thyroid cell type to its embryologic origin?
o: Follicular cells — endoderm (pharyngeal floor); parafollicular cells — 4th pharyngeal pouch
Follicular cells — mesoderm; parafollicular cells — ectoderm
Follicular cells — 4th pharyngeal pouch; parafollicular cells — endoderm of pharyngeal floor
e: Correct. Follicular cells come from endoderm; parafollicular cells arise from the 4th pharyngeal pouch.
The 3rd pouch forms the thymus and inferior parathyroids.
Neither origin is correct.
The origins are reversed.
Neither follicular nor (in First Aid) parafollicular cells are listed as neural crest.

q.s: An adult has an asymptomatic midline cystic mass at the level of the thyrohyoid membrane. Fine-needle aspiration shows thyroid follicular epithelium. What should be checked before excision?
o: That a normal thyroid gland exists in the neck
e: Correct. If the ectopic tissue is the only thyroid tissue, removing it causes hypothyroidism, so imaging should confirm a normal gland.
Glucose is unrelated.
Catecholamines are relevant to adrenal medullary tumors.
Calcitonin is a C-cell marker, not relevant to a thyroglossal remnant.
Calcium is unrelated to the cyst's origin.

q.s: A 3-year-old has a midline neck cyst that becomes red and tender during an upper respiratory infection. The infection most likely reached the cyst through:
o: A fistula to the external ear canal
A connection to the pyriform sinus
Lymphatic drainage from the lateral neck
Its persistent connection to the tongue base via the duct
e: A 1st cleft anomaly connects to the ear canal.
3rd/4th pouch sinus tracts open into the pyriform sinus and lie laterally.
Lymphatic spread causes cervical adenitis, a lateral process.
Correct. The thyroglossal duct remnant communicates with the foramen cecum, so oral flora can infect the cyst.
Hematogenous seeding of this cyst is not the usual route.

q.s: Which feature most suggests that a neck mass is a thyroglossal duct cyst rather than a thyroid nodule?
o: It is located in the lower neck beside the trachea
It is lateral to the sternocleidomastoid
e: That location fits a thyroid lobe nodule.
A lateral location argues against a thyroglossal cyst.
Thyroglossal cysts are usually cystic.
Correct. Elevation with tongue protrusion reflects attachment to the tongue via the duct.
Thyroid nodules also move with swallowing because the gland is attached to the larynx.

q.s: Thyroid tissue found within an ovarian teratoma (struma ovarii) contrasts with the usual developmental ectopia. In normal development, where is ectopic thyroid tissue most often found?
o: In the lateral cervical lymph nodes
Along the descent path, most often in the tongue
Along the descent path, most often in the mediastinum
e: Thyroid tissue in lateral nodes suggests metastasis.
The adrenal is not on the thyroid's descent path.
Correct. Ectopic thyroid most often lies along the path of descent, most commonly as lingual thyroid.
The posterior pituitary is neuroectodermal and unrelated.
The mediastinum is less common than the tongue.
